title: Workload skew & SLA playbook kickoff - AurigaPay
summary: Kickoff to scope a 2-week PoC focused on workload skew, tail latency gating, and replay-based benchmarking. Customer seeks a playbook: target throughput and concurrency maps, token distribution profiling, and clear pass/fail criteria (p50/p95/p99 latency targets + correctness checks). Agreement to run initial replay of 48 hours traffic sample, a synthetic burst test to 3x expected QPS, and a follow-up benchmark with Redwood SE present. Action items: Redwood to share benchmark template, security docs (SOC 2+SAML/KMS notes), and initial cost estimates; Customer to provide 72-hour traffic export and list of priority endpoints.
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark plan + sample JMeter/LW replay instructions (by 2026-06-17)
Customer to upload 72h traffic export to secure bucket and share link (by 2026-06-19)
Schedule 4-hour benchmark window w/ Diego and AurigaPay ops (week of 2026-06-22)
Redwood to share security/compliance packet and draft NDA (by 2026-06-16)
action_items: Maya Chen: Send benchmark template and pricing estimate (due 2026-06-17)
Diego Ramos: Prepare baseline test harness and replay script; define synthetic burst scenario (due 2026-06-19)
Priya Kapoor: Export 72h production traffic sample and tag priority routes (due 2026-06-19)
Sofia Marin: Provide SOC2 attestation and high-level network architecture for VPC peering questions (due 2026-06-18)
transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we just want to make sure we capture AurigaPay's goals for the POC. Can you quick intros?
[00:00:23] Priya (AurigaPay): Sure I'm Priya head of payments, Liam's our platform lead and Sofia covers security. We basically want to validate that Redwood can handle our busiest checkout flows with predictable tail latency and also check isolation for PCI adjacent data.
[00:00:45] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, Diego here, I'll be hands-on for the bench and replay. Quick question up front: when you say "busiest checkout flows" what's peak QPS and typical payload sizes?
[00:01:02] Liam (AurigaPay): Peak for a single endpoint is around 250 qps in spikes, sustained is closer to 60-80 qps. Average input tokens per request are small — around 20 to 50 tokens — but outputs are variable, often 90 to 180 tokens for the user-visible response. There's also a long-tail of multi-step conversations that have larger sessions.
[00:01:29] Maya: That's super helpful. So we should size for burst capacity to 3x peak initially — that covers safety margins and degraded fallback. Any concurrency targets you're expecting?
[00:01:42] Priya: In total across all endpoints during peak we see around 1,200 concurrent in flight, but for the core checkout flow it's about 350 concurrent.
[00:01:53] Diego: Perfect. For the PoC we typically run three bench phases: cold/steady-state replay from your 72h sample, then a synthetic burst to 3x peak, then a long-tail session test to exercise KV cache and prefix hits. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and also token emissions per response.
[00:02:16] Sofia: Security question — we need to confirm whether logs have PIi, and how Redwood handles KMS/HSM integration since some data may be tokenized. Also SAML SSO for the console is a gating item.
[00:02:30] Maya: Understood, we'll include our SOC 2 overview and KMS integration guide. SAML SSO is a standard integration for the Console; we can draft the metadata exchange.
[00:02:45] Priya: Ok good. Back to SLA — we need to define pass/fail. Our internal goal is p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 900ms for the checkout route under production-like load. If p99 spikes above that under replay, the PoC doesn't meet expectations.
[00:03:05] Diego: Noted. Those are aggressive but achievable depending on model size and quantization. Which model families are you planning to use? In-house distilled or open LLMs?
[00:03:18] Liam: We're on a hybrid plan — open LLM for most responses, same family as Mistral-ish but custom fine-tune for our prompts. We also evaluate a smaller distilled model for very low-latency confirmations.
[00:03:33] Maya: That aligns with typical Redwood flows — we can route requests to a faster quantized variant for confirmations and to a larger model for complex cases. For the PoC we'll test both variants and measure unit costs.
[00:03:47] Priya: Cost is a big factor. We need at least an estimate for per-1M token cost across the two model variants and also an estimate of how batching/caching changes that.
[00:03:58] Diego: We'll provide a cost sensitivity table. In the bench we'll capture tokens_in, tokens_out, and tokens_per_second, and run a cost model that assumes your traffic mix. Also we'll demonstrate Redwood Optimize suggestions: quant profiles and batching thresholds.
[00:04:15] Liam: On telemetry — we need per-route traces, token-level cost breakdown, and a CSV of request latencies. Is that available in the PoC?
[00:04:25] Diego: Yes, we can enable detailed tracing for the benchmark window, with per-request token counts and GPU utilization metrics. We'll produce dashboards and a zipped CSV export after the run.
[00:04:39] Priya: Nice. A couple of corner cases: we sometimes get conversational back-and-forths causing token spikes mid-session. How does Redwood handle KV cache eviction under high concurrency?
[00:04:53] Diego: We'll instrument cache hit/miss rates during the replay. The runtime uses a KV caching policy per session; eviction behavior depends on concurrency and memory pressure. Part of the long-tail test is to reproduce those session patterns to quantify degradation.
[00:05:10] Sofia: For compliance, we need audit logs for every inference request and the option to disable retention for certain routes. Can you do route-level retention toggles?
[00:05:22] Maya: Yes, route-level retention and token redaction options exist in Private and Dedicated; for hosted we'll show how to configure retention controls and redaction heuristics. We'll include that in the security packet.
[00:05:36] Priya: Great. What's the expected PoC timeline?
[00:05:40] Maya: Proposal: 1 week to exchange traffic + security docs, 1 week to run and analyze benchmarks — so two weeks total. We can compress if you have a ready traffic export.
[00:05:52] Liam: We can probably get the 72h export by Friday if you need it sooner.
[00:05:57] Maya: Excellent. Diego, can you walk through the exact bench scenarios you plan to run?
[00:06:03] Diego: Sure — Scenario A: Replay 72h traffic at original timestamps (scaled to a 48h window to fit the run) to capture steady-state and diurnal patterns. Scenario B: Synthetic burst — ramp to 3x observed peak over 5 minutes, hold 10 minutes, then decay; capture p99 tail and resource saturation. Scenario C: Long-tail session test — replay multi-turn sessions sequenced to stress KV cache and memory. For each scenario we log per-route latencies, concurrency, GPU metrics, and token counts. We'll also run a node failure to test graceful degradation.
[00:06:49] Priya: Node failure test is important. We want graceful fallback to a cheaper region or model variant.
[00:06:56] Maya: We can include a controlled fallback policy test: simulate instance OOM and ensure routing to fallback model or region keeps success rate above 98%.
[00:07:06] Liam: For the replay — is there a recommended format? We use gzipped JSON lines containing timestamps and raw request payloads.
[00:07:14] Diego: That's perfect. We'll provide a small schema and a sample script to transform your logs into the replay format.
[00:07:22] Priya: On evaluation — besides latency, we need a correctness pass: some outputs are legal-sensitive and must not hallucinate. Can Redwood run automated evals against a gold set?
[00:07:35] Diego: We can run a semi-automated eval where we score responses against your gold set for a subset of requests; full manual QA is usually recommended for the legal-critical flows. We'll include a template for the evaluation metrics.
[00:07:48] Priya: Sounds good. Anything else on security?
[00:07:52] Sofia: SAML metadata, KMS endpoints, and whether service-to-service traffic stays in the customer VPC for Private deployments. Also we need a disclosure on who can see request-level logs in Redwood's console.
[00:08:06] Maya: We'll include a section on RBAC and audit logs — default is minimal, you can restrict by role, and for Private we support customer-controlled KMS. We'll put this in the packet Diego mentioned.
[00:08:16] Liam: About cost again — will you provide a runbook for expected unit costs under different batch sizes?
[00:08:23] Diego: Yes, the cost sensitivity table will include batch size, tokens per second, GPU utilization, and per-1M token estimate. We'll also recommend batching thresholds that preserve p99 latency under your targets.
[00:08:37] Priya: Ok so to confirm pass/fail: if replay under production-like concurrency meets p50/p95/p99 and the correctness sample has >98% pass, then PoC is a success. If p99 is over 900ms or correctness below 95% we fail. Is that fair?
[00:08:54] Maya: That sounds like a clear gating criteria; we'll capture that in the follow-up doc.
[00:09:02] Priya: One more operational note: during peak days we have a bursty payment partner traffic that causes short lived 10x spikes for a few minutes. Can you run a spike test that mimics that?
[00:09:14] Diego: Yes, we'll design a "microburst" script to replay those short 10x spikes and measure tail effects.
[00:09:21] Priya: Great. Any blockers from Redwood?
[00:09:24] Maya: None on our side aside from receiving the traffic export and security contacts. We'll send the template and schedule link.
[00:09:33] Liam: We'll aim to have the export and the list of priority routes by Friday.
[00:09:39] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with action items and the benchmark plan. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:46] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:58:00] (call ended)
notes: Customer emphasizes p99 gating and legal-sensitive correctness tests
Replay + synthetic burst + long-tail session tests agreed
Security packet and SAML/KMS details required before bench
